rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work
rows.verified: Work-related violence includes abuse, threats or assault in circumstances relating to work.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work
rows.verified: Work-related violence can include verbal abuse, online abuse, telephone threats and physical attacks.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work
rows.verified: Employers must protect workers from work-related violence so far as reasonably practicable.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work
rows.verified: Employers must assess significant violence risks and implement effective controls.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work
rows.verified: Workers and their representatives should be consulted when violence risks are assessed.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work
rows.verified: Where violence risks cannot be removed, employers should use a combination of suitable control measures.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work
rows.verified: Violence incidents should be recorded, reviewed and used to improve controls.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work
rows.verified: Employers should provide suitable support to workers affected by violence or aggression.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work
rows.verified: Violence controls depend on the work activity, location, lone-working arrangements, public contact and incident history.

rows.source: HSE violence and aggression at work
rows.verified: Workplace-violence evidence is activity- and organisation-specific and is not an exact parcel-level violence probability.

rows.source: HSE young people at work
rows.verified: Employers have the same general health, safety and welfare responsibilities for workers under 18 as for other workers.

rows.source: HSE young people at work
rows.verified: Young people may be at greater risk because they lack experience, maturity or awareness of workplace hazards.

rows.source: HSE young people at work
rows.verified: Employers should review risk assessments before a young person starts when existing arrangements do not already address their needs.

rows.source: HSE young people at work
rows.verified: Young workers need clear and sufficient instruction, training and supervision.

rows.source: HSE young people at work
rows.verified: Training should be proportionate to the risks and the tasks the young person will perform.

rows.source: HSE young people at work
rows.verified: Employers should check that young workers understand workplace hazards and precautions.

rows.source: HSE young people at work
rows.verified: Young people may need more supervision than experienced adult workers.

rows.source: HSE young people at work
rows.verified: Young people must not be exposed to risk because of lack of experience, lack of awareness or lack of maturity.

rows.source: HSE young people at work
rows.verified: Controls depend on the young person's maturity, capability, health, task, environment, training and supervision.

rows.source: HSE young people at work
rows.verified: Young-worker evidence is person-, task- and workplace-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
